messages:
Priya S.: FYI — we started getting a flurry of 503/500s on hosted inference around 09:10 UTC. Multiple customers (ACME, FinSecure) filed support tickets — CS-12894 / CS-12897. Initial look: upstream inference workers are restarting frequently (container restarts + segfaults). Posting notes here so eng/sre can triage.

Marc L. (oncall): I'm pulling logs now. Alerts show p95 errors jumped from ~0.5% to 18% across region us-west1. I can repro some 503s hitting the gateway which then returns upstream 502/503. Investigating worker pods.

Jon P.: On it. Can someone dump the pod list and restart counts? Also, did we roll any runtime or kernel changes in the last 24h? I see a runtime push to v10.4.2 at ~03:00 UTC in the deploy feed.

Emma K.: Pod list and restart counts:
```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep worker
inference-worker-7f8d4   1/1     Running   5 (4d23h)   10.128.4.12   gpu-node-3   <none>
inference-worker-bc13a   1/1     Running   12 (2h)     10.128.4.18   gpu-node-5   <none>
```
worker-bc13a restarted 12x in the last 2 hours. Logs show repeated segfaults and OOM traces. Pasting log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:21Z] INFO Serving request id=rc-9f3
[2026-03-15T09:12:22Z] ERROR runtime: fatal error: unexpected signal during runtime execution
[2026-03-15T09:12:22Z] SIGSEGV: segmentation violation
[2026-03-15T09:12:22Z] goroutine 1 [running]:
...
Segmentation fault (core dumped)

[2026-03-15T09:12:23Z] E GPU: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T09:12:23Z] E Worker: failed to allocate kv cache: requested=1.4GiB available=1.2GiB
```

Marc L. (oncall): Also grabbed dmesg from the node, shows repeated OOM-killer messages targeting the worker container. nv top shows GPU mem pinned near 98% before crash.

Priya S.: Support notes that most failing requests are large-context completion jobs (8k+ tokens) and some batched requests. Could be a regression with the attention kernel + quantized model path.

Jon P.: That matches a change in v10.4.2 — we shipped an optimized attention kernel for long sequences on quantized int8 to speed up throughput. Hypothesis: memory accounting bug for combined KV cache + attention scratch buffer causing oversubscription on certain batch/seq combinations.

Emma K.: Repro steps I used against staging (to replicate):
1) POST to /v1/generate with model redwood-llama-70b-q8 and sequence_length=8192 and batch_size=4 and streaming off.
2) Observe worker process memory climb until segfault or cuda OOM in ~30-90s.
3) kubectl logs shows same stacktrace (segfault) and then kube restarts pod.

Repro commands:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"model":"redwood-llama-70b-q8","max_tokens":8192,"batch":4,"prompt":"<long prompt>"}'
kubectl logs -n inference inference-worker-bc13a -c worker --since=30m
```

Marc L. (oncall): Mitigation applied:
- Scaled up worker pool in us-west1 by +3 pods (to shift load away from offending nodes).
- Added routing rule to fallback to redwood-llama-70b-fp16 for requests with seq_len > 4096 until fix.
- Temporarily pinned runtime to v10.4.1 in the canary router for hoste d customers.

DeployBot: Rolled back runtime canary to v10.4.1 at 09:40 UTC (canary=0.2 -> 0.0). No manual approval required for emergency rollback.

SupportBot: Noted mitigation in CS tickets CS-12894/CS-12897, notified ACME support contact and increased SL priority to P1.

Jon P.: I reproduced locally and bisected to commit abc1234 in runtime repo which adjusted buffer accounting in attention_kernels.cu. I can craft a hotfix but need infra to collect core dumps and GPU memstats from impacted pods for debugging.

Emma K.: Core dumps disabled by default. I'll enable coredump collection on a small set of nodes and add a crashloop collector job. Also added a liveness probe tolerance to avoid immediate restarts while we collect artifacts.

Priya S.: Customer impact summary for comms: ~12 customers experienced transient 503s, 3 customers saw degraded throughput with retries. No data leakage. Support will send update within 1 hour. Logging for affected requests attached in tickets.

Marc L. (oncall): Short-term plan:
- Keep rollback in place (v10.4.1), continue routing fallback for long sequences.
- Collect core dumps + nvml mem stats (Emma)
- Patch and smoke test hotfix (Jon)
- Postmortem + deploy a test that fuzzes large seq + batch combos in CI (owner: eng-runtime)

Jon P.: Patch is drafted (PR #4823), adds fixed buffer accounting + unit test. Will test on staging with stress harness (seq=8192 batch=4) and then coordinate hotfix deploy to canary. ETA 3h.

Emma K.: Monitoring/alerts to create:
- GPU memory high watermark per pod (alert at 90%)
- Frequent container restarts per pod (alert if >5 in 30m)
- OOM/segfault signatures in worker logs -> page to oncall
I'll open infra tickets.

Priya S.: Thanks — I'll keep comms updated and escalate any new customer P1s. Please post when the canary hotfix goes live so I can update tickets.

DeployBot: Hotfix canary deployed (runtime v10.4.3-canary) at 12:05 UTC to 10% of traffic.

Jon P.: Canary looks clean after 30m stress run. No OOMs. Rolling to 50% then full after 60m.

Marc L. (oncall): Marking this thread for postmortem and timeline capture. Need a short incident report for customers. Assigning owners: Postmortem (Jon), Monitoring (Emma), Customer comms (Priya). Will follow up with RCA once PR merged.

Priya S.: CS tickets updated, customers notified of root cause hypothesis and mitigation. Will send a status update after full rollout.

(reacts: :thumbsup: from Jon P., :eyes: from Emma K.)
